# Testimonial & case study request

Ask two weeks after launch. Early enough that it's fresh, late enough that
they've seen it working.

---

## Why most testimonial requests fail

"Would you write me a testimonial?" puts the work on the client — they have to
decide what to say, and writing about someone else is oddly hard. Most people
say yes and then never do it.

Give them the questions instead. Three specific prompts get a usable answer in
five minutes.

---

## The email

> **Subject:** A small favour
>
> Hi [NAME],
>
> Hope the site's settling in well — [SOMETHING SPECIFIC YOU'VE NOTICED:
> "nice to see the enquiry form getting used" / "the new journal posts look
> great"].
>
> Would you write me a couple of sentences I can use? The most useful ones
> answer three things:
>
> 1. What was the problem before we started?
> 2. What was working together actually like?
> 3. What's different now?
>
> Three lines is plenty — don't polish it, I'd rather it sounded like you.
>
> And if you'd be up for a short case study — a few numbers, a couple of
> screenshots, twenty minutes on a call — I'd be glad to do that too. You'd
> get a link back from a site that ranks reasonably well.
>
> Either way, thanks for a good project.
>
> [YOUR NAME]

---

## If they say yes to a case study

### Questions to ask on the call

**Before**
- What was the situation before? What specifically wasn't working?
- What had you tried?
- What made you decide to do something about it?

**Choosing**
- What made you get in touch with me?
- Was there anything you were unsure about?
- What made you decide to go ahead?

> The hesitation question is the most valuable one you'll ask. Whatever made
> them nervous is making your next prospect nervous too — and now you can
> address it on your own site.

**During**
- How did you find the process?
- Anything that surprised you?

**After** — push for numbers
- What's changed since launch?
- Any numbers you can share? Enquiries, sales, time saved, calls avoided?
- What's the best thing about it now?
- Would you recommend me? What would you say?

### What to collect

- [ ] Quotes, verbatim
- [ ] At least one **number**
- [ ] Screenshots — before and after
- [ ] Logo, with permission to use
- [ ] Name, role, company, headshot
- [ ] **Written approval to publish**

---

## Case study structure

Keep it to a page. Nobody reads a long one.

```
[CLIENT] — [ONE-LINE RESULT WITH A NUMBER]

The situation
    Two or three sentences. What was wrong, in their words.

What we did
    Three or four sentences. Focus on decisions, not deliverables.
    "We cut the site from 30 pages to 9" beats "we built a WordPress site".

The result
    Numbers first. Then the quote.

    "[THE BEST QUOTE FROM THE CALL]"
    — [NAME], [ROLE], [COMPANY]

[SCREENSHOTS]

Want something similar? [CTA]
```

---

## A number is worth ten adjectives

"Enquiries went from 4 a month to 15" does more work than any amount of
"professional, responsive, a pleasure to work with".

If they genuinely have no numbers, use a time or effort measure: "updating the
site went from a day of my time to ten minutes", "we stopped fielding the same
question on the phone".

---

## Where to use it

- [ ] Website — testimonials near the pricing or contact section
- [ ] Proposal — the "why me" section
- [ ] Case study page
- [ ] Google Business profile _(ask them to leave it there too)_
- [ ] LinkedIn recommendation
- [ ] Sales calls — "a client of mine had exactly this problem…"
